The fresh measurements confirm the matrix-free opportunity: eight illuminations take about 7.5× as long as one, while selected LU barely changes. Doubling the cluster from 512 to 1,024 spheres takes almost exactly 4× as long, with six GMRES iterations in both cases. That points to shared translation work and better scaling with particle count as the main targets. The current CPU path is also substantially faster than the archived timings, so the old GPU speedups need remeasurement.

I’ll focus on end-to-end CPU gains for realistic workloads, starting with shared translation work and periodic sums. I’ll measure the current release build, pursue the strongest candidates, and keep changes only when they preserve accuracy and improve complete workflows.

One useful boundary is clearer now: batching makes the matrix-free solver much faster, but reusing a dense factorization can still win when it fits in memory. In the 512-sphere check, a fresh matrix-free solve took about 99 ms versus 267 ms for dense factorization plus solve; with the dense factor already available, its solve took only 8 ms.
